# Incident Report — MTA 2026-02-28 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |

| IPv4 | 10.2.28.88 | Consistent source across all suspicious flows |
| MAC | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad | ARP (frame data) and DHCP client-id `010019d1b24dad` bound to 10.2.28.88 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR | DHCP option 12 hostname; NBNS registrations for `DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR<00>/<20>` from 10.2.28.88 |
| Domain | easyas123.tech (AD domain EASYAS123) | Kerberos/LDAP traffic to 10.2.28.2 (EASYAS123-DC.easyas123.tech), NBNS workgroup name EASYAS123 |
| Logged-in user | brolf | Kerberos `CNameString` = `brolf` in AS-REQ traffic from 10.2.28.88 to DC 10.2.28.2 |

Gateway: 10.2.28.1. Domain controller: 10.2.28.2.

## Malware Family
**NetSupport Manager RAT** (NetSupport RAT), attribution is **behavioral** (no IDS/Suricata alert file was provided in the evidence directory — only the pcap was present).

Behavioral basis:
- HTTP `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` on every C2 request.
- Application-layer protocol keywords decoded directly from the TCP payload match the known NetSupport client/gateway protocol: outbound `CMD=POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1\n` and inbound `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<hex-encoded blob>`.
- Beaconing cadence: POST to `/fakeurl.htm` roughly every 60 seconds for the entire ~4.3-hour capture (550 packets on the stream), to a single external IP addressed literally by dotted-quad in the HTTP Host/request-line, not a hostname — a classic NetSupport RAT C2 fingerprint.
- Traffic runs on TCP/443 but is **plaintext HTTP**, not TLS (confirmed: zero TLS records on that stream) — another NetSupport RAT tell (it reuses port 443 without encryption).

No delivery artifact (dropper, phishing document, exploit) is observable in this capture — the beacon to the C2 IP begins within the first minute of the trace (relative time ~44.9s), immediately after the host resolves the C2 domain. The initial infection/dropper stage occurred outside the captured window.
